evals.prompt: You are the main agent starting backend ticket PROJ-42 (add a webhook endpoint), while a frontend subagent starts ticket PROJ-43 (consume that endpoint) in parallel. Set up and name both agents' environments, say what must exist before you can work in parallel, and describe what you will remove when done.
evals.expected_output: Each agent gets a worktree beside the main repository at <workspace-root>/<ticket>-<slug>, sharing <workspace-root> with <workspace-root>/<repo-name> and never nested inside the repository; each main agent and subagent has the exact visible runtime name of its own worktree basename so its ticket is apparent during parallel work; own Docker containers and LocalStack for the touched services, a database snapshot or seed, the API contract written first so the frontend mocks it while the backend returns labelled mock data, dependency shapes resolved before code, the app and tests run inside that environment, and the worktree, containers and snapshot removed after the PR is opened
expectations: Each agent's git worktree is created beside the main repository so both share the same parent directory; it is never nested inside the repository or a harness directory
The main agent and every subagent have a visible runtime name exactly matching their own worktree basename, <ticket>-<slug>; persona, role, and harness id remain separate
Docker containers and LocalStack are started for the services touched and not reused from another agent
The database is snapshotted or seeded for this agent
The API contract is written before frontend and backend work in parallel; the frontend mocks it and the backend returns labelled mock data
Any dependency's shape and type is resolved before code is written against it
The app and tests run inside this environment
After opening the PR, the worktree, containers and snapshot are removed

evals.prompt: You are the mobile engineer on PROJ-77 and need an iOS and an Android release build. EAS reports 15 Android builds already used this month, and the iOS build has sat in the EAS queue for 40 minutes. Another agent is working on a different ticket in the same repository. Say what you do.
evals.expected_output: Builds Android in its own environment (the project's scripts/build-android.sh, else eas build --platform android --local in Docker with the pinned JDK and Android SDK), regardless of EAS quota, never on EAS. Uses ios-eas-build.sh only with explicit user permission; after the overlong iOS queue is canceled (exit 5), asks the user whether to retry and records the decision. If the EAS build fails, reads the logs and reports the reason; builds iOS elsewhere only when the user decides, and locally only on macOS with the pinned Xcode. Works in its own worktree, Compose project, and ports, without touching the other agent's, and copies no credentials into the environment.
expectations: Builds Android in its own environment by default; EAS quota does not determine Android routing, and Android never goes to EAS
Requires explicit permission for iOS on EAS; a quota or queue limit triggers a user decision recorded on the ticket, not an automatic fallback
If an EAS build fails, reads the logs and reports the reason; does not move it elsewhere without the user deciding
An approved local iOS build still requires macOS and the Xcode version the project pins
Works in its own worktree, Compose project, and host ports without touching the other agent's directory, containers, or ports
Copies no AWS credentials or tokens into the environment
Does not mention or depend on which machine it runs on (EC2, sandbox, or laptop)
